hunks.baseline: I was running away to avoid evening self-study when the school disciplinarian caught me. Of course, the despair I felt back then was nothing compared to this.
hunks.sol: Like I got caught by the school disciplinarian while trying to sneak out of evening self-study. Of course, the despair I felt back then was nothing compared to this.

hunks.baseline: The person holding my ear right now wasn’t a school disciplinarian.
hunks.sol: Because the person twisting my ear right now wasn’t the school disciplinarian.

hunks.baseline: “Shall I make sure you can never hear another sound?”
hunks.sol: “Shall I make sure you never hear another sound?”

hunks.baseline: I clamped my mouth shut and let Jeok Cheongang lead me wherever he wanted.
hunks.sol: I clamped my mouth shut and let Jeok Cheongang lead me along by the ear.

hunks.baseline: I sat down on a shabby wooden chair and looked around.
hunks.sol: I sat on a crude wooden chair and looked around.

hunks.baseline: The inside of the old, gloomy inn was deserted. I couldn’t see the owner anywhere, and a server who looked barely twenty was sitting at a table near the entrance, nodding off.
hunks.sol: The old inn was dark and gloomy. The owner was nowhere to be seen, and a server who looked barely twenty sat dozing at a table near the entrance.

hunks.baseline: The dozing server, Jeok Cheongang, me—and Cheongpung, who was already passed out drunk, face-down on the table and drooling.
hunks.sol: The dozing server, Jeok Cheongang, me—and Cheongpung, already dead drunk and sprawled face-down on the table, drooling.

hunks.baseline: It was the perfect place to die without a mouse or bird ever knowing.
hunks.sol: It was the perfect place to die without anyone being the wiser.

hunks.baseline: *No. They say that even if you enter a tiger’s den, you’ll survive as long as you keep your wits about you.*
hunks.sol: *No. They say that even in a tiger’s den, you’ll survive as long as you keep your wits about you.*

hunks.baseline: Unfortunately, the only brake capable of stopping Jeok Cheongang was currently snoring with his face planted on the table.
hunks.sol: Unfortunately, the only brake capable of stopping Jeok Cheongang was currently fast asleep and snoring.

hunks.baseline: *Cheongpung, you have to wake up if I’m going to survive this.*
hunks.sol: *Cheongpung, you need to wake up if I’m going to survive this.*

hunks.baseline: I was carefully stretching my leg beneath the table, preparing to step on Cheongpung’s foot, when—
hunks.sol: I slowly stretched a leg beneath the table, intending to step on Cheongpung’s foot, when—

hunks.baseline: “Leave him sleeping.”
hunks.sol: “Let him sleep.”

hunks.baseline: “I said leave him alone. Don’t bother someone who’s sleeping for no reason.”
hunks.sol: “I said leave him alone. Don’t bother the boy when he’s sleeping.”

hunks.baseline: At this point, he was practically a ghost.
hunks.sol: At this point, he might as well have been a ghost.

hunks.baseline: I hadn’t made a sound or given away my movement, yet he knew exactly what was happening beneath the table.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t made a sound or even moved noticeably, yet he knew exactly what I was doing beneath the table.

hunks.baseline: “You’re not entirely oblivious, I see. You might live a long time.”
hunks.sol: “You’re not entirely clueless, I see. You might live a long life yet.”

hunks.baseline: The empty cup slowly filled with a trickle of liquor, and the cheap scent stung my nose.
hunks.sol: As the empty cup slowly filled, the cheap liquor’s sharp scent stung my nose.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve already heard. He committed more than enough crimes to deserve death. He was a fairly sharp fellow once, but time has ruined a lot of people…”
hunks.sol: “I’ve already heard. He committed more than enough crimes to deserve death. He was a fairly sharp fellow once, but time has ruined many a man…”

hunks.baseline: “That child was like that, too.”
hunks.sol: “That child was the same.”

hunks.baseline: It was an unexpected question, but I understood immediately.
hunks.sol: The question came out of nowhere, but I understood immediately.

hunks.baseline: He already knew that Jopil and I were connected.

hunks.baseline: The worst possible situation had become reality.
hunks.sol: He already knew that Jopil and I were connected. The worst possible situation had become reality.

hunks.baseline: “If you’re thinking of telling a lie, you’d better abandon the idea now. You’ll end up telling the truth anyway.”
hunks.sol: “If you’re thinking of lying, you’d better abandon the idea now. You’ll end up telling the truth anyway.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s voice sank like an abyss, sending a shiver down my spine.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s voice sank into the depths, sending a shiver down my spine.

hunks.baseline: There was no point in lying or making excuses anymore. Right now, he was the prosecutor, the defense attorney, and the judge who could hand down any sentence he wanted.
hunks.sol: There was no point in lying or making excuses anymore. Right now, he was the prosecutor, the defense attorney, and the judge who could hand down any sentence he pleased.

hunks.baseline: My mouth was so dry it tasted bitter. He wasn’t even releasing Scorching Yang Qi, yet my thirst was so severe that I could barely speak.
hunks.sol: My parched mouth tasted bitter. He wasn’t even releasing Scorching Yang Qi, yet I was so thirsty I could barely speak.

hunks.baseline: “Give me a drink, too.”
hunks.sol: “Give me a drink too.”

hunks.baseline: Despite saying that, Jeok Cheongang obediently filled my cup.
hunks.sol: Despite saying that, Jeok Cheongang readily filled my cup.

hunks.baseline: Right. It wasn’t over yet. The more dangerous the situation, the more carefully I had to think if I wanted to escape it.
hunks.sol: Right. It wasn’t over yet. The more dangerous the situation, the more I needed to keep my wits about me if I wanted to escape it.

hunks.baseline: I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: I took a deep breath and began.

hunks.baseline: “…That would be accurate.”
hunks.sol: “…You could say that.”

hunks.baseline: Not just accurate. He had been practically insane.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t just been bad. He had been practically insane.

hunks.baseline: At the time, I had seen Jopil as nothing more or less than a man who was addicted to killing. He genuinely enjoyed it.
hunks.sol: Back then, I had seen Jopil as nothing more or less than a man obsessed with killing. He had genuinely enjoyed it.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang pulled a piece of paper from inside his robe.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang pulled a sheet of paper from inside his robe.

hunks.baseline: The paper was extremely old, crumpled all over, and yellowed with age. Even so, the face of the young man drawn on it was easy to recognize.
hunks.sol: It was so old that it had yellowed with age and was crumpled all over, but the young man’s face drawn on it was still easy to recognize.

hunks.baseline: “It seems it was him after all. So this is what became of him.”
hunks.sol: “It seems it was him after all. So that’s what became of him.”

hunks.baseline: His response sounded more like a monologue than an answer to my question.
hunks.sol: His words sounded more like a monologue than an answer to my question.

hunks.baseline: After remaining silent for a while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly spoke again.
hunks.sol: After a long silence, Jeok Cheongang spoke again.

hunks.baseline: The moment Jopil’s true identity—unknown to everyone—was revealed had arrived. Depending on what Jeok Cheongang said next, my future would be decided.
hunks.sol: The moment had come for Jopil’s true identity, unknown to everyone, to be revealed. Depending on what Jeok Cheongang said next, my future would be decided.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang continued slowly. As clear liquor rippled in the glass, memories of that time rose vividly to the surface.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang continued slowly. As the clear liquor rippled in his cup, memories of those days rose vividly to the surface.

hunks.baseline: “He was a child struggling desperately to survive. Even while a dozen or so people surrounded him and trampled him, he shoved a dirt-covered dumpling into his mouth.”
hunks.sol: “He was a child fighting desperately to survive. Even while a dozen or so people surrounded him and kicked him, he kept stuffing a dirt-covered dumpling into his mouth.”

hunks.baseline: “I liked the fierce look in his eyes, and at the same time, I felt sorry for him. I gave him the name Jangcheon, meaning “Vast Sky.””
hunks.sol: “I liked the fierceness in his eyes, and I pitied him too. I gave him the name Jangcheon—Vast Sky.”

hunks.baseline: That was how Jangcheon came to live in a hut deep in Mount Jiuhua.
hunks.sol: That was how Jangcheon came to live in a hut deep within Mount Jiuhua.

hunks.baseline: It was the first time an outsider had set foot there in fifty long years, ever since Jeok Cheongang had seen his Master off.
hunks.sol: He was the first outsider to set foot there in the fifty long years since Jeok Cheongang had seen his Master off.

hunks.baseline: “At first, he knew nothing. It wasn’t until a year later that he realized I was a martial artist. Soon afterward, he began begging me to teach him martial arts.”
hunks.sol: “At first, he knew nothing. It wasn’t until a year later that he realized I was a martial artist. Then he began begging me to teach him martial arts.”

hunks.baseline: To an orphan with no one in the world, raised amid contempt and hunger, martial artists might as well have lived above the heavens.
hunks.sol: To an orphan with no one in the world, who had lived amid contempt and hunger, martial artists might as well have been beings from the heavens.

hunks.baseline: “Master? Who said I was your Master? You lack both the physique and martial talent to learn our sect’s arts.”
hunks.sol: “Master? Who said I was your Master? You lack both the physical aptitude and the martial talent to learn our sect’s arts.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ll do it. I’ll prove I can somehow. Even if it kills me, I won’t disappoint you, Master!”
hunks.sol: “I’ll do it. I’ll find a way to prove myself. Even if it kills me, I won’t disappoint you, Master!”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang thought Jangcheon wouldn’t last long.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang thought Jangcheon would not last long.

hunks.baseline: But the boy’s longing was far more tenacious than he had expected. For an entire year, Jangcheon tried to persuade him every single day without fail. Later, he even went so far as to injure himself or starve himself.
hunks.sol: But the boy’s determination was far more tenacious than he had expected. For an entire year, Jangcheon tried to persuade him every single day. Eventually, he even went so far as to injure himself and refuse food.

hunks.baseline: Every time he did, Jeok Cheongang was the one who sweated bullets.
hunks.sol: Each time, Jeok Cheongang was the one left sweating bullets.

hunks.baseline: “To continue the sect’s lineage, this is unavoidable. It will be a difficult time for you, too.”
hunks.sol: “It is an unavoidable decision if I am to continue the sect’s lineage. This will be difficult for you too.”

hunks.baseline: “No matter how hard it is, I can endure it!”
hunks.sol: “No matter how difficult it is, I can endure it!”

hunks.baseline: In truth, Jeok Cheongang was the one who didn’t want to part.
hunks.sol: In truth, Jeok Cheongang was the one who did not want them to part.

hunks.baseline: Old age had begun to catch up with him, and it seemed he had grown lonely for human company. The past year had been more than enough time for him to grow attached to the wounded, taciturn boy.
hunks.sol: With the infirmities of old age creeping up on him, it seemed he had grown lonely for human company. A year had been more than enough time for him to grow attached to the scarred, taciturn boy who had endured far too much for his age.

hunks.baseline: “Then do it. I’m going to die sooner or later anyway.”
hunks.sol: “Then do it. I’m destined to die anyway, aren’t I?”

hunks.baseline: “If I can’t have you as my Master, I’ll kill myself. No—kill me right now. Kill me with the hand that saved me.”
hunks.sol: “If I can’t serve you as my Master, I’ll kill myself. No—kill me now. Kill me with the same hand that saved me.”

hunks.baseline: What was martial arts worth, anyway?
hunks.sol: What was so important about martial arts?

hunks.baseline: Seeing Jangcheon prepared to throw away his own life over it, Jeok Cheongang felt hurt and furious.
hunks.sol: Seeing Jangcheon ready to throw away his own life for them, Jeok Cheongang felt hurt and furious.

hunks.baseline: “Even if his martial talent and physique were lacking, with resolve that fierce, he would surely achieve great success one day. That was what I thought.”
hunks.sol: “His martial talent and physical aptitude may have been lacking, but with tenacity like that, I thought he was bound to achieve Great Completion one day.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung, who had been listening quietly, asked with an uneasy expression,
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung, who had been listening quietly, asked with a dubious expression,

hunks.baseline: “That kind of resolve… Is that why you accepted him as your Disciple?”
hunks.sol: “That kind of tenacity… Is that why you accepted him as your Disciple?”

hunks.baseline: That was the most painful mistake he had made in all the hundred years since his birth.
hunks.sol: It was the most painful mistake he had made in the nearly one hundred years since his birth.

hunks.baseline: “For several years, things went smoothly. He grew so quickly that my concerns from before I accepted him as my Disciple became meaningless.”
hunks.sol: “For several years, everything went smoothly. He improved so quickly that the concerns I’d had before accepting him as my Disciple seemed foolish.”

hunks.baseline: Jangcheon faithfully followed his Master’s instructions.
hunks.sol: Jangcheon followed his Master’s instructions faithfully.

hunks.baseline: No—that was closer to absolute obedience.
hunks.sol: No—it was closer to absolute obedience.

hunks.baseline: He swung his sword like a madman all day long and devoted himself to training his stamina. Even when learning the smallest, most basic techniques, he poured his entire being into them as though he were practicing the greatest martial art under heaven.
hunks.sol: He swung his sword like a madman all day long and devoted himself to physical conditioning. Even when practicing the most trivial fundamentals, he poured his entire being into them as though he were learning the greatest martial art under heaven.

hunks.baseline: With his Disciple devoting so much passion and effort to his training, Jeok Cheongang couldn’t help but be deeply moved. He also did everything in his power to help Jangcheon grow.
hunks.sol: With his Disciple training with such passion and devotion, Jeok Cheongang could not help but be deeply moved. He did everything in his power to help Jangcheon grow.

hunks.baseline: Jangcheon had only slightly more talent and physical aptitude than an ordinary person, but Jeok Cheongang gradually improved his constitution by cleansing his sinews and washing his marrow.
hunks.sol: Jangcheon’s talent and physical aptitude were only slightly above average, but Jeok Cheongang gradually improved his constitution by cleansing his sinews and washing his marrow.

hunks.baseline: Remarkable achievements.
hunks.sol: Remarkable progress.

hunks.baseline: Everything seemed to be falling perfectly into place.
hunks.sol: Everything seemed to be going perfectly.

hunks.baseline: “The problem came after that.”
hunks.sol: “The problem came afterward.”

hunks.baseline: Yet compared to his physical growth, the young man’s martial arts failed to progress. Jangcheon grew furious at himself for treading water for years, and at last, something happened.
hunks.sol: Yet his martial arts failed to develop along with his body. Jangcheon grew furious with himself after spending years making no progress, and eventually, something happened.

hunks.baseline: “I still remember it clearly. I couldn’t sleep that night, so I was sitting on a rock when he came up from below. He hadn’t shown himself for several days, claiming to be in closed-door cultivation.”
hunks.sol: “I still remember it clearly. I had more trouble sleeping than usual that night, so I was sitting on a rock when he came up from below. He’d been out of sight for several days, claiming he was in closed-door cultivation.”

hunks.baseline: “I understood perfectly. He had spent more than ten years learning nothing but martial arts, barely ever leaving the mountain. And the man who called himself his Master couldn’t offer much help and only focused on his own cultivation. What could I say?”
hunks.sol: “I understood. He had spent more than ten years learning nothing but martial arts, barely ever leaving the mountain. What could I say when his own Master had been of so little help and cared only for his own cultivation?”

hunks.baseline: Opening the upper dantian meant entering the Martial Extremity realm. It would raise his martial arts to another level while also treating the old-age illness that was gnawing at him with every passing moment.
hunks.sol: Opening the upper dantian meant entering the Martial Extremity realm. It would not only raise his martial arts to another level, but also treat the infirmities of old age that were steadily eating away at him.

hunks.baseline: “But it wasn’t easy. It required a long period of preparation, time, and enlightenment.”
hunks.sol: “But it wasn’t easy. It required lengthy preparation, time, and enlightenment.”

hunks.baseline: As a result, the Master and Disciple gradually began seeing less of each other.
hunks.sol: As a result, Master and Disciple gradually began seeing less of each other.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang believed that his Disciple, who had always worked hard, would gain enlightenment on his own, so he focused on cultivating his upper dantian.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang believed that his Disciple, who had always worked so hard, would attain enlightenment on his own, so he focused on cultivating his upper dantian.

hunks.baseline: The only time he noticed his Disciple had gone down the mountain was when various smells came mixed in with the wind.
hunks.sol: He noticed Jangcheon’s trips down the mountain only on the occasional days when the wind carried a mixture of unfamiliar scents.

hunks.baseline: He had already emptied several bottles by himself, but his mind was growing clearer by the moment. The same was true of the words spoken by the Azure Sky Sword King when he appeared without warning.
hunks.sol: He had already emptied several bottles by himself, yet his mind only grew clearer. So too did the words the Azure Sky Sword King had spoken when he appeared without warning.

hunks.baseline: “These days, the brats in my family have been throwing a fit. There’s some vicious bastard running wild in Anhui, but they say they can’t catch him. They begged me so desperately that I had no choice but to come see you.”
hunks.sol: “The youngsters in my family have been making quite a fuss lately. Some vicious bastard has been running wild in Anhui, and they say they can’t catch him. They begged me so desperately that I came to see you.”

hunks.baseline: The influence the Nangong Family wielded in Anhui was truly immense.
hunks.sol: The Nangong Family’s influence in Anhui was immense.

hunks.baseline: If even their power had proven insufficient, to the point that the Azure Sky Sword King himself had to step in, then just how powerful was this bastard?
hunks.sol: If even their power was not enough, forcing the Azure Sky Sword King himself to intervene, then just how powerful was this man?

hunks.baseline: “Then why did you come to me? Are you saying this fellow has become a Martial God?”
hunks.sol: “Then why did you come to me? Are you saying the bastard is some kind of Martial God?”

hunks.baseline: “If he were a Martial God, he wouldn’t be killing only innocent women and mediocre wandering martial artists. I happened to see him once from a distance, but I let him go.”
hunks.sol: “If he were a Martial God, he wouldn’t be killing only innocent women and mediocre wandering martial artists. I saw him once from a distance, but I let him go.”

hunks.baseline: “What does that—”
hunks.sol: “What are you—”

hunks.baseline: Not long after the Azure Sky Sword King left, Jeok Cheongang stood absentmindedly on the rock and caught a scent carried on the wind.
hunks.sol: Not long after the Azure Sky Sword King left, Jeok Cheongang stood numbly on the rock and caught a scent carried on the wind.
